# orrery.live

> An interactive 3D solar system in the browser. Real planet positions computed from JPL orbital data, comets, spacecraft, a naked-eye star background with constellations, and a time machine covering 3000 BC to 3000 AD. Free, no account, no adverts.

orrery.live shows where the planets are right now, or on any date you choose. Drag to orbit the view, scroll to zoom, and step time forwards or backwards to watch conjunctions, alignments and retrograde loops play out. It includes the eight planets and their major moons, dwarf planets, notable comets, and the trajectories of spacecraft such as the Voyagers and New Horizons. Famous planetary alignments and historical events are bookmarked so you can jump straight to them.

Positions are computed client-side from JPL Horizons ephemeris data in the J2000 reference frame, with correct planetary spin axes. The star field is the HYG catalogue, and constellation lines are from d3-celestial.

Technical: static site built on three.js, MIT licensed, installable PWA that works offline once loaded. Textures from Solar System Scope (CC BY 4.0); star catalogue CC BY-SA 4.0.

## Links

- [Orrery](https://orrery.live/): the app
- [Night sky tonight](https://orrery.live/night-sky/): sky map of tonight from the visitor's own location: which planets are visible after dark, when they are best placed and which way to look, with sunset/sunrise and twilight times, the Moon's phase, 1,637 stars and the 88 constellations; scrub through the night, change date or city, or point a phone at the sky to identify what is there (compass corrected for magnetic declination); covers 1000 to 3000 AD (most accurate 1800 to 2200); runs entirely in the browser, and the location stays on the device unless the visitor chooses to share a link with their exact position (ordinary share links use the nearest town)
- [Where are the planets right now](https://orrery.live/now/): live table of every planet's distance from the Sun and Earth, light time, evening or morning sky, retrograde motion and next opposition, with a top-down map
- [Planetary alignments and planet parades](https://orrery.live/planetary-alignment/): upcoming and past planet parade dates (2022 to 2040) with the planets involved, what an alignment really is (and what a syzygy is: three or more bodies in a nearly straight line), and links into the orrery
- [Where is Halley's Comet now](https://orrery.live/halleys-comet/): live distance from the Sun and Earth, speed and a to-scale map of Halley's orbit; its next perihelion (28 July 2061, on Earth's side of the Sun), famous returns since 240 BC, and its two annual meteor showers
- [What is an orrery?](https://orrery.live/what-is-an-orrery/): the meaning and pronunciation of "orrery", how mechanical orreries work (gear ratios, why they cannot be to scale), kinds of orrery, and their history from the Antikythera mechanism to today
- [The perfect alignment?](https://orrery.live/perfect-alignment/): whether all eight planets ever line up in a perfect syzygy; the tightest groupings in 6,000 years (1596 BC, 40°), in 20,000 years of JPL data (5753 AD, 39°) and in a million-year N-body search (863337 AD, 17°); how the rarity scales with the angle (within 30° every ~65,000 years, 20° every ~700,000, 10° every ~40 million, 5° effectively never) and how far ahead any date can be trusted
- [Sitemap](https://orrery.live/sitemap.xml)

## Related

- [whatsacross.com](https://whatsacross.com/): click any coast on a 3D globe and see what lies across the water in every direction, by the same author
- [Adam's Arcade](https://games.adamwoodland.com/): all of the author's free browser games and tools
- [Adam Woodland](https://adamwoodland.com/): the author, an OT/ICS cybersecurity consultant; this site is a side project
